records.claim_scope: Uniform eventual trivial conjugate intersection for every pair of soluble subgroups in Sn and An; first question only.
records.prior_work_relation: Earlier positive result covers soluble maximal subgroups, while the official posted full result is from this same project.
qualifications: No priority certificate from bounded search.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: Existence of an infinite group with ordinary spread exactly one, realized by the diagonal subgroup of Thompson’s F.
records.prior_work_relation: Lower bound is a specialization of Golan-Polak’s published generation theorem; upper bound uses her fixed-point obstruction.
qualifications: Credit these substantial prior ingredients prominently.
Potential novelty is the exact ordinary-spread-one corollary, not the generation theorem.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: Every rational-linear group with finitely many full abstract automorphism orbits is virtually soluble; stronger finite-index normal torsion-free nilpotent conclusion.
records.prior_work_relation: Located predecessors impose structural, rank, residual-finiteness or finite-generation assumptions absent from the local statement.
qualifications: Arbitrary, including infinitely generated, rational-linear subgroups must remain in scope.
Existing broader local context audit supplements the fresh major-theorem recheck.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: A finitely generated dense subgroup of the infinite iterated wreath product of natural degree-five A5, with subexponential growth.
records.prior_work_relation: Brieussel’s checked construction requires local degrees >= 29; Woryna’s compatible degree-five construction has exponential growth.
qualifications: Amenability is insufficient for this question.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: A semiabelian group of order 2592 that is not monomial.
records.prior_work_relation: Kida’s order-192 example disproves the converse; his order-96 complement/subgroup pair is an explicitly credited prior input.
qualifications: No novelty claim for the general character-transfer mechanism.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: Finite transitive soluble action and two distinct points such that every transporter fixes exactly one point.
records.prior_work_relation: Muliarchyk’s paper is a complete independent negative solution with a smaller witness.
qualifications: Neither earlier private commits nor present HTTP Last-Modified resolves first public solution.
Preserve existing independently constructed Lean counterexample outside the discovery catalogue.
Do not state that Muliarchyk solved it first.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

records.claim_scope: A parameter-free first-order formula on a residually finite integer Heisenberg group has a finite value set generating an infinite subgroup.
records.prior_work_relation: Prior positive results concern existential formulas or different group families and retain the general question.
qualifications: Scope is first-order formulas, not the separate word-conciseness question.
The local formula has a universal quantifier, outside the existential theorem.
records.proof_correctness_gate: separate audit; not certified by novelty review

sources.title: The Kourovka Notebook: repository
primary_claims_read: Current selective repository of solution papers; links for 21.3(a), 21.68 and Muliarchyk 21.99 inspected.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Positive evidence of listed solutions; absence of a link is not proof of novelty.

sources.title: Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri and Burness: On the regularity number of a finite group and other base-related invariants
primary_claims_read: Conjecture 2 in v2: eventual regularity number two for soluble subgroups of symmetric and alternating groups.
The positive soluble-maximal-subgroup theorem at degree at least 17 is narrower.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Original conjecture and partial theorem, not a complete solution for arbitrary soluble subgroups.

sources.title: The soluble-intersection limit in Sn
primary_claims_read: Theorem 1.1: sharp limiting proportion exp(-9/2).
Alternating corollary and eventual positive answer.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Own result, not an independent competitor; only first question admitted.

sources.title: Gili Golan-Polak: Thompson’s group F is almost 3/2-generated
primary_claims_read: Theorem 2 and Proposition 16(1): prescribed nonzero endpoint exponents yield a companion generating the full inverse image of the lattice of endpoint vectors.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Specializing the companion endpoint vector to (1,1) gives spread at least one for the diagonal subgroup. Substantial prior theorem must be credited.

sources.title: Gili Golan-Polak: The spread of Thompson’s group F
primary_claims_read: Introduction: existence of an infinite group of ordinary spread exactly one remains open.
Lemma 2: fixed-point obstruction to generation.
Remark 11: nonnegative product of endpoint exponents forces an interior fixed point.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Contains ingredients for the upper bound after a diagonal specialization; no explicit ordinary-spread-one conclusion located.

sources.title: Bastos, Dantas and de Melo: soluble finite-rank groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
primary_claims_read: Theorem A, page 2, assumes solubility and finite rank.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Does not deduce virtual solubility from arbitrary rational linearity and finite automorphism-orbit count.

sources.title: Bastos, Dantas and de Melo: nilpotent and virtually soluble groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
primary_claims_read: Theorem 1.2, page 2, assumes virtual nilpotence.
Corollary 1.3, page 3, assumes virtual solubility and finite rank.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Hypotheses include the structural condition the local result must prove.

sources.title: Dantas, de Melo and Kato: On soluble groups of finite rank with finitely many automorphism orbits
primary_claims_read: Introduction, page 2341, and all three main statements, page 2342, read in user-supplied publisher PDF.
Theorem 1.1: mixed-order soluble finite-rank groups with four orbits.
Theorem 1.2: mixed-order metabelian finite-rank groups with four orbits.
Theorem 1.3: mixed-order soluble finite-rank groups with five orbits.
sources.relation_to_local_result: All statements retain hypotheses absent from the rational-linear question.

sources.title: Dantas and de Sousa: groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
primary_claims_read: Theorem A concerns residually finite groups.
Theorem B concerns finitely generated locally graded groups.
Theorem C concerns specified rational nilpotent completions.
sources.relation_to_local_result: None settles arbitrary rational-linear subgroups; (Q,+) shows residual finiteness cannot be assumed.

sources.title: de Melo and Kato: full unitriangular groups and automorphism orbits
primary_claims_read: Results concern full unitriangular groups and orbit counts; broader classification discussed.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Related nilpotent classification, not arbitrary rational-linear virtual solubility.

sources.title: Jérémie Brieussel: doctoral thesis, sections 3.6.1–3.6.7
primary_claims_read: Printed pages 76–80; construction hypotheses and Propositions 3.6.1, 3.6.3, 3.6.6 and Remark 3.6.7.
Eligible generator construction used by the intermediate-growth theorem requires all local degrees at least 29.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Does not specialize to natural degree-five A5 action.

sources.title: Adam Woryna: dense amenable subgroups of inverse limits of iterated wreath products
primary_claims_read: Corollary 2 applies to the degree-five alternating action but expressly produces exponential growth.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Amenability and contraction do not supply subexponential growth.

sources.title: Eberhard, Maini, Sabatini and Tracey: diameter and iterated wreath products
primary_claims_read: End of section 9 in both v1 and current v2 repeats exact degree-five question.
Lower growth restriction rules out some slow subexponential rates, not all subexponential growth.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Contemporary source continues to formulate the exact question; no competing full construction.

sources.title: Masanari Kida: On semiabelian groups
primary_claims_read: Conjecture 1.3 asks semiabelian implies monomial.
Theorem 1.4 gives an order-192 monomial group that is not semiabelian, disproving the converse.
Page 710 gives an order-96 semiabelian group containing SL2(3).
sources.relation_to_local_result: Supplies the prior complement/subgroup input but no nonmonomial semiabelian counterexample.

sources.title: solution to Kourovka Problem 21.68
primary_claims_read: Theorem 1 gives the order-2592 semiabelian nonmonomial example and credits Kida’s input.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Own construction, not an independent competitor.

sources.title: Kyrylo Muliarchyk: A counterexample to Problem 21.99 of the Kourovka Notebook
primary_claims_read: All four pages read.
Theorem 1: a soluble group of order 46,875,000,000 acts faithfully and transitively in degree 23,437,500; two distinct points have 2000 transporters and every transporter fixes exactly one point.
Sections 2–4 supply construction and fixed-block calculation for every transporter.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Complete independent negative solution to the exact statement. Smaller than local witness. Public priority unresolved; current file modification time is not first-publication evidence.

sources.title: Conte and Petschick: Conciseness of first-order formulae
primary_claims_read: Question 1 asks the residually finite question; parameter-free convention read.
Existential-formula positive theorem is 1.2 in preprint and 1.1 in journal.
Journal version retains Question 1.
sources.relation_to_local_result: Existential theorem does not cover local existential-universal-existential formula.

sources.title: Ciobanu and Conte: Concise formulae in groups of non-positive curvature
primary_claims_read: Introduction describes positive partial progress on the general question.
Results concern acylindrically hyperbolic groups and existential formulas.
sources.relation_to_local_result: No Heisenberg two-value full counterexample is recorded.
